images.title: One tenth split into ten parts
images.purpose: Show that splitting each tenth of a unit into 10 parts gives 100 small parts, each one hundredth.
images.composition: One large 10 by 10 square grid at the centre-left with three short labels at its right; everything else is white space.
exact_structure: A large square representing 1 unit, divided into a 10 by 10 grid of 100 small equal squares with thin grey (#6B7280) lines.
Exactly one column (the second from the left) is highlighted as 1 tenth: its 10 small squares, 9 amber (#E69F00) and the bottom one reddish purple (#CC79A7).
To the right, three labels with thin leader lines: one to the whole square (1 unit = 100 parts), one to the amber column (1 tenth = 10 parts), one to the single purple square (1 part = 1/100).
rejection: more or fewer than one highlighted column, or the purple square is outside that column
the highlighted column has other than 10 squares
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Splitting every tenth into 10 gives 100 equal parts in a unit, each one hundredth.
images.description: A 10 by 10 grid with one column of ten squares highlighted and one single square marked as a hundredth.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Look at one column first (a tenth), then at one small square inside it (a hundredth).

image_decisions.why: The grid makes 10 × 10 = 100 and the size of one hundredth visible at once.
